victory_line: Three smiles! I'm so proud of you. Kind of. Pretty much. Now get out of my break room.
defeat_line: Three bad jokes. Everyone's still sad. Well, tomorrow's another day.

lines.text: Ah, the new guy! Welcome to Smiling Friends. We're a small company with a big mission: making people smile.
Your first assignment is easy. You have to make THREE clients smile. Three. Not one more, not one less... well, more is fine.
Choose your words carefully. Screw up three times and the company loses faith in you. And so do I. No pressure.
Go get 'em, champ! The world isn't going to smile by itself.

intro.text: Hi, I'm Natasha. Alan said he'd meet me here. He keeps saying he's busy. I thought tonight might be different.

rounds.prompt: I got all dressed up for him. Do I look "stood up" to you?

choices.text: You look great. Alan missed out on a fun night.
choices.reply: Aww... HEH! I mean, tee-hee!

choices.text: Maybe he's just running late?
choices.reply: Two hours late? Yeah. Sounds like Alan.

choices.text: Yeah, kind of.
choices.reply: Wow. Thanks.

rounds.prompt: I've been trying to get Alan to hang out for months. He keeps slipping away. It's starting to feel personal.

choices.text: Are you sure this is about a date? You sound like his landlord.
choices.reply: His landlord? What? No. I just... know where he lives. Heh. You're quick.

choices.text: Maybe you could ask him to hang out somewhere else.
choices.reply: I tried. He said the park was too far. It's across the street.

choices.text: Why do you have a beard?
choices.reply: I don't have a beard! It's... a shadow. From the disco ball.

rounds.prompt: Let's dance. Maybe if I have a good night, Alan will finally want to hang out with me. Just once.

choices.text: I dance like Alan when you call: straight for the exit.
choices.reply: HAHAHA! He does! But I think he almost waved last time.

choices.text: Okay, just one little step.
choices.reply: One little step. Maybe Alan would do one too.

choices.text: I don't dance.
choices.reply: And Alan won't hang out. What a night.

laugh_line.text: HAHAHA! Okay, you got me. I'm not Natasha. I'm Alan's landlord. I set this up because he keeps dodging me. I just want to hang out with the guy! Tell him I'm still here.

fail_line.text: Well, that didn't work. Maybe Alan will want to hang out next time. I should probably take this wig off.

intro.text: Welcome to my forest. Hello. This is my new son, Froggy. Hello. He used to be Glep. Hello.

rounds.prompt: Glep glorp! Glep! (Translation: help me, he makes me eat flies.)

choices.text: Don't worry, Glep. We're getting you out of here!
choices.reply: Nobody leaves the forest. Hello. But I like your attitude. Hello.

choices.text: So how are the flies?
choices.reply: Glep! (Crunchy. Don't tell anyone.)

choices.text: I can't understand a word he says.
choices.reply: GLEP! (There are subtitles!)

rounds.prompt: Frogs don't pay taxes. Hello. Frogs don't go to work. Hello. Is this not the perfect life? Hello.

choices.text: Honestly? You're the king of this forest, Mr. Frog.
choices.reply: King of the forest. Hello. I will need a crown. Hello.

choices.text: The no-taxes thing does sound nice.
choices.reply: The government cannot find me here. Hello.

choices.text: This is a kidnapping.
choices.reply: This is a legal adoption. Hello. There is paperwork. Hello.

rounds.prompt: Make me laugh and Froggy can go home. Hello. Tell me a frog joke. Hello.

choices.text: What's a frog's favorite drink? Croak-a-Cola!
choices.reply: HAHAHA! Croak-a-Cola! Hello! That is terrible! Hello!

choices.text: Ribbit, ribbit.
choices.reply: Ribbit. Hello. Your accent is good. Hello.

choices.text: Frogs aren't funny.
choices.reply: Take that back. Hello. Froggy, bite him. Hello.

laugh_line.text: GLEP GLEP GLORP! (I'm free! Thank you!)

fail_line.text: Froggy stays with me. Hello. Come back with a better joke. Hello.

intro.text: Yeah. I'm Desmond. I called because everything feels kind of pointless. I don't know. You can try.

rounds.prompt: I got up, looked around, and couldn't think of a reason to do any of it. So... now you're here.

choices.text: You know what you need? A rollercoaster. Come on, my treat.
choices.reply: A rollercoaster. Sure. I haven't got anything else going on.

choices.text: Well... one day at a time, right?
choices.reply: Yeah. I know. There are a lot of them.

choices.text: I don't know, honestly.
choices.reply: Right. Same.

rounds.prompt: We rode it. I yelled. Now I'm standing here. Still feels pretty much the same.

choices.text: You screamed the whole way down. That's not nothing!
choices.reply: Yeah. I screamed. That's something, I guess.

choices.text: Want to go again?
choices.reply: Maybe. Not right now.

choices.text: Well, that was a waste of money.
choices.reply: Yeah. I figured you'd say that.

rounds.prompt: Maybe I expected a ride to fix everything. That's stupid. I still feel stuck.

choices.text: You're not broken. You came out today, rode Dave Rollercoaster three times and kept that cotton candy. That's a guy who wants to stick around.
choices.reply: ...I kept the cotton candy. Didn't have to, I guess. Maybe I do want another day.

choices.text: Everyone feels broken sometimes.
choices.reply: Maybe. Doesn't make this part go away.

choices.text: Maybe you are.
choices.reply: Yeah. Probably.

laugh_line.text: Hey. It's Desmond. I got a job, and I don't hate it. Things still get weird sometimes, but I'm doing okay. I wouldn't have gone on that ride if you hadn't shown up. So... thanks. - Desmond.

fail_line.text: Well. Thanks for trying, I guess.
